display.purpose: The one big Besley line per screen: a song's key, a scale's name, the sing-setup title, a finished run's time.

headline.purpose: Bottom-sheet titles and full-screen step titles.

title.purpose: Section heads and the song title.

subhead.purpose: Sans headings inside sheets and switch labels.

lede.purpose: The plain-words line under a display line or section head, Second Ink, max 62ch.

small.purpose: Explanations and ladder captions, Second Ink.

fine.purpose: Fine print: source notes, privacy notes, secondary explanations, Third Ink.

caption.purpose: Rung step words, nav labels (600), time tags (700).

note.purpose: Note names on the ladder; list notes and chords run 750 at 1.25-1.375rem.

chord.purpose: Chord names in the loop bars; songbook names at 1.5rem.

fact.purpose: Fact values in the margin and singing-ladder note labels.

solfa.purpose: Syllables (do re mi) in Besley italic; upright white 650 inside the cobalt column, 850 at home.

numeral.purpose: Roman numerals under chords, Besley italic in Second Ink.

timer.purpose: The run clock (m:ss.s) and best times, tabular lining figures.

shadows.name: ledge
shadows.purpose: Under the go button only: a hard 2px ink ledge with a short soft fall; collapses when pressed. The artwork thumbnail uses the same ledge at 1px.

shadows.name: ledge-dark
shadows.purpose: The ledge in the dark scheme.

shadows.name: sheet
shadows.purpose: The bottom sheet rising over the chart, above a rgba(8, 11, 20, 0.45) backdrop.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The system's one easing curve, for the unroll and every utility transition.

motion.name: unroll
motion.purpose: The one authored moment: the ladder unrolls downward (clip-path inset reveal) whenever its key or scale changes.

motion.name: pointer-step
motion.purpose: The pointer steps rung to rung in time with each played note.

motion.name: pointer-flash
motion.purpose: How long a tapped rung stays lit.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Buttons drop 1px on press (the go button 2px, onto its ledge).

motion.name: color
motion.purpose: Background and shadow changes; the sheet backdrop fade.

motion.name: sheet-rise
motion.purpose: The bottom sheet rises 24px and fades in.

motion.name: step-nudge
motion.purpose: The yellow pointer on the analysis step in progress nudges 4px.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Under prefers-reduced-motion every animation and transition collapses to 1ms and one iteration.

narrative.overview:
The Modulator was the Tonic Sol-fa classroom wall chart: a tall column of syllables, with the neighboring keys in columns beside it, that a teacher pointed at while the class sang. Musician rebuilds it as a phone instrument. Song analysis, scale study, and singing all hang from the same vertical pitch ladder, a cobalt column whose white rungs are spaced by real half steps, so the distance between two notes is visible before it is sung. Pitch is always height. The system refuses the category's grid of cards and its round tuner dial.

The surface is a printed chart, not an app skin. A cool chart-white sheet carries navy-black ink; ink binding-tape bands close the top and bottom of the screen; sections open with ruled ink lines instead of boxes. Besley, a Clarendon slab, letters everything musical at poster weight (keys, notes, chords, numerals, syllables, times) while the phone's own sans runs the controls. Color is spent only as meaning: cobalt is the ladder and home, pointer yellow is "here, now, you", and green and vermilion are the away and tension jobs of chords. Density is calm and one-handed: one column on the phone, 48px targets, the go button within reach of the thumb.

Light and dark both ship, following the system color scheme. The light chart is the native printed object; the dark chart deepens the sheet to night navy and keeps every ink's role. Motion is one authored moment, the ladder unrolling downward like a pull-down chart, plus the pointer stepping from rung to rung with the sound; reduced motion collapses all of it.
keyCharacteristics: One vertical pitch ladder anchors every musical screen; rung spacing is the real interval.
Flat chart-white sheet, navy ink, ink binding-tape bands top and bottom, ruled sections instead of boxes.
Besley (Clarendon slab) letters the music and the headings; the system sans runs the interface.
Color is meaning: cobalt is the ladder and home, pointer yellow is here/now/you, green is away, vermilion is tension.
Square chart edges: 4px on controls and inline panels; bands, ladders, bars, and sheets stay square.
Light and dark both ship; the light chart is the native object.

rules.name: The Pointer Rule
rules.body: Pointer yellow means "here, now, you": the note to sing, her voice while it is in tune, the rung the pointer is on, the hold bar filling as she lands a note, and her best time. It is lent only to the one go button in view, focus rings, the active-nav bar, and pointer-shaped marks (the brand mark, the analysis step in progress, the changed note on a neighbor-key column). It never fills headings or panels, never marks a chord job, and never marks home.

rules.name: The Home Is Cobalt Rule
rules.body: Home is always cobalt: the heaviest rung on the cobalt column with its label in Cobalt Ink at weight 850, the home dots on the fretboard, the home chord job. Yellow is where she is; cobalt is where the scale rests.

rules.name: The Three Jobs Rule
rules.body: Chords have exactly three colored jobs (home cobalt, away green, tension vermilion), and a job color never speaks alone: every colored tag is lettered with its chord name, and every list that explains jobs prints the job word (Home, Away, Tension, Borrowed, Leading, Outside) beside a 10px square swatch. Borrowed, leading, and outside chords take a dashed gray outline, never a fill. Lettering on a job fill must reach 4.5:1: the light chart's white lettering does (5.2:1 to 6.8:1); the dark chart's white-on-fill tags currently measure 3.5:1 (away), 4.3:1 (tension), and 4.45:1 (home) and are not yet part of the system.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Besley letters the music and the chart's headings: every note, key, chord, numeral, syllable, and time, and every display, headline, and title line. The system sans runs everything that operates the app: button labels, tabs, form labels, explanations, step words. A note name never appears in the sans; when a button's label is a note, key, or chord, that label is Besley.

rules.name: The Engraved Accidental Rule
rules.body: Sharps and flats beside a note or chord name in type are engraved Bravura glyphs at 0.82em, and screen readers hear "F sharp". Tiny SVG labels and plain-words sentences use the ♯ and ♭ characters. Never a typed "#" or "b". Octave numbers drop to 0.55em sans in Third Ink.

rules.name: The Ladder-Left Rule
rules.body: When a screen shows a scale, its ladder is the leftmost column and everything else is margin notes beside or below it. The ladder never sits in a card, a carousel, or a right-hand column.

rules.name: The Printed Plane Rule
rules.body: Panels, lists, notices, and ladders never float: no drop shadows, blur, or glass on them. Depth is tone and ink; the ledge and the sheet are the whole shadow vocabulary.

rules.name: The Square Chart Rule
rules.body: Never round a button, chip, field, tag, panel, or sheet past 4px; sheets that slide over the chart stay square. Notation's own circles and capsules are exempt.

rules.name: The One Go Rule
rules.body: At most one go button is visible at a time, and it always carries the step from reading to singing: "Sing this scale", "Start timed run".

rules.name: The One Moment Rule
rules.body: The unroll is the system's only authored animation, and the pointer stepping with the sound is its only traveling mark. Utility motion stays short on the same ease-out (presses 120ms, color 160ms, sheets 260ms), and reduced motion collapses every animation and transition to 1ms: the chart arrives unrolled, sheets appear in place, and the pointer simply marks each sounding rung.

dos: Do hang every scale on the Modulator: a cobalt column, white rungs spaced by real half steps (30px per half step; 20px in the song view on phones), syllables on the rungs, note names in the margin.
Do keep pointer yellow for here, now, and you (the note to sing, the in-tune voice, the active rung, the best time) plus the one go button, focus rings, and the active-nav bar.
Do make home cobalt wherever it appears: the heavy home rung, Cobalt Ink home labels, cobalt fretboard dots, the home chord job.
Do pair every job color with a chord name or a job word, and give borrowed, leading, and outside chords a dashed gray outline.
Do letter notes, keys, chords, numerals, syllables, times, and headings in Besley with engraved accidentals; run controls and explanations in the system sans.
Do divide the sheet with ink: 1.5px rules to open sections, 1px faint rules between rows, tape bands at the top and bottom.
Do put Fixed Ink (#131a2e) on yellow and on white tags in both schemes.
Do ship light and dark together, keep every role in both, and hold lettering on job fills to 4.5:1 in both.
Do collapse every animation and transition under reduced motion.
donts: Don't show pitch as a round tuner dial, needle, or gauge; pitch is height on the ladder.
Don't box sections or list items as cards (raised, shadowed, or tiled); the only outlined panels are notices and the analysis panel.
Don't use pointer yellow for headings, panel fills, or decoration, for any chord job, or for home; the pale Pointer Wash behind coaching notices is its only tint.
Don't let a job color carry meaning alone, or fill a borrowed, leading, or outside chord.
Don't round a button, chip, field, tag, panel, or sheet past 4px; notation's circles and capsules are exempt.
Don't draw the fretboard as wood or texture; it is ink frets and strings on Label White.
Don't add drop shadows, blur, or glass to panels, lists, notices, or ladders.
Don't add a second authored animation; the unroll and the pointer are the motion.
Don't type "#" or "b" for an accidental.
